nature: pre-registration only; it authorizes nothing by itself. A separate A5 verdict on this exact dossier and a Lead GO record with matching SHAs are required before any solver start.

search_space.selection_rule: chosen from the measured 12D CDi response audit (sweep_1 max|dCDi| 1.707e-3, sweep_2 6.977e-4, wing_area 1.45e-10); NOT chosen from any meta-learning result

bootstrap.method: LHS on the frozen box, baseline forced first

evaluation_recipe.start_2: 13-point refinement centred on the coarse quadratic CL(alpha) root, +/-0.024 deg at 0.004 deg resolution
evaluation_recipe.charge_policy: both starts and all internal alpha cases are charged even when the design ends infeasible; retries are never allowed

admission_rule.authority: admit_real_manifest re-reads the raw bytes and requires an ACTUAL polar row satisfying |q*Sref*CL - L_ref|/L_ref <= 1e-3; interpolated rows are never promoted
admission_rule.objective: Di_N = q * Sref * CDi of that admitted raw row
admission_rule.sref: per-design, recomputed from the actual geometry

stop_conditions: the baseline design (bootstrap design 0) fails: the batch aborts at once and the remaining budget is not spent, because a baseline failure means the protocol rather than the aerodynamics is broken
any spendable cap reached (12 designs, or the 24 starts and 240 internal cases that the design cap implies; the stored 36-start ceiling is unreachable)
two consecutive designs with no solver result at all
three consecutive designs with no admitted raw row: the loop stops with budget deliberately unspent (at most 6 charged starts) instead of grinding out 12 misses
upload + remote readback after every 8 starts or 60 minutes, before continuing
deliverables: raw_cases/ with every case's .vsp3/.vspgeom/.vspaero/.polar/.history/.adb, decks, mesh/wake, stdout/stderr, exit code and timeout flag
tables/all_evaluations.csv, admitted_labels.csv, failed_or_null.csv, optimization_history.csv, acquisition_trace.csv, actual_solver_ledger.csv
tables/resource_usage.csv + figures with CPU and memory during the optimization

final_aircraft/ with baseline.vsp3, optimized.vsp3, design_before_after.csv, optimized_design.json, performance_before_after.csv, constraint_report.json, verification_receipt.json, figures/ and the independent O0-FINAL re-run
SHA256SUMS.txt, data_manifest.json and a GitHub readback audit

o0_final.rule: the final candidate must be an admitted, non-baseline design; it is re-run with a fresh case_id and an empty directory, and the baseline is re-run the same way
o0_final.repeatability: same frozen configuration, two independent re-runs

design_selection.baseline: the admitted row flagged is_baseline (bootstrap design 0)
design_selection.best: the admitted non-baseline row with the lowest Di_N of the optimizer batch, which is the objective being maximised downward
design_selection.when_identities_are_fixed: the selection rule is fixed here, before any batch runs; the two design identities and the batch result SHA256 are bound by the separate O0-FINAL GO record, because a design id cannot be written into a pre-registration that precedes the batch that produced it

separate_budget.note: this is a separately itemized verification ledger; it is never folded into the O0 optimizer caps, and the wake probe cases are never admitted because the admitted wake count is fixed at 8. The budget covers the whole of the verification step, including the three starts the crashed first attempt already spent, because a replacement batch that ignored them would need nine starts and would misreport what the verification actually cost.
itemization: 2 void rows: the baseline repeats the crashed first attempt spent at 2 wake nodes, below the admission mesh of 8; already paid for, never admissible, never re-run, 13 alpha cases each = 26 internal cases

1 wake-probe start already spent: the baseline solved at 16 wake nodes, which completed before the crash and whose paid output is on the disk; never admitted, not re-run, 13 alpha cases = 13 internal cases
4 repeat starts still to spend: baseline and best at the reference mesh, two independent re-runs each, 13 refinement alpha cases per start = 52 internal cases
1 wake-probe start still to spend: the best design at 16 wake nodes, never admitted, 13 alpha cases = 13 internal cases
26 + 13 + 52 + 13 = 104 internal cases, and 2 + 1 + 4 + 1 = 8 starts in total, of which 3 starts are already spent
separate_budget.why_it_is_not_extra_optimizer_budget: the optimizer cap is a search budget; these repeats cannot propose or admit a new design, they can only measure two already-selected ones again

authorization.may_start_only_after: the optimizer batch is closed by a batch record; a verification start spent while the optimizer is still running would be unauditable
authorization.ledger_must_survive_a_crash: the ledger is written after every charge and read back on start-up, so a run that dies after three starts restarts owing three
authorization.no_repeat_of_a_charged_label: one label is one case; spending a second start for a label already in the ledger is refused rather than silently double-charged

row_kinds.repeat: a reference-mesh repeat of one of the two designs; it may be admitted
row_kinds.wake: a 16-wake-node probe; it can never be admitted, because the admission mesh is fixed at 8 wake nodes
row_kinds.void: a start already spent on a mis-configured case; it is charged so the bill matches the disk, it is never admitted, and it is never re-run. The kind is set by the plan entry and is never inferred from a wake count, which is exactly how the first attempt mislabelled two repeats as probes

repair_of_the_first_verification_attempt.what_happened: the first attempt at section 4b died on its third start with 'wake probe cap exceeded: 2 rows'. The two rows that had been charged were the baseline repeats, and they had been charged as kind=wake because the runner derived the kind from the wake count and gave every repeat 2 wake nodes instead of the admission mesh of 8
repair_of_the_first_verification_attempt.what_was_already_spent: 3 real solver starts and 39 internal alpha cases: final-baseline-r1 and final-baseline-r2 at 2 wake nodes, and final-baseline-wake16 at 16 wake nodes, which completed with its polar and case_result.json still on the disk
repair_of_the_first_verification_attempt.what_was_wrong_with_the_ledger: it recorded 2 starts and 26 internal cases, both mislabelled kind=wake, and it was missing the third start entirely, because the charge happened after the run instead of before it
what_the_repair_changes: the kind is now a plan field, never derived from a number
the charge happens before the solver is spawned, so a crash cannot lose a paid start, and a crash after a charge writes a record next to it
the two mislabelled repeats are re-charged as void rows with the sha256 of the polar and case_result.json that back them
the completed 16-wake-node probe is charged as a wake row, not re-run
the budget becomes 8 starts and 104 internal cases, of which 3 starts and 39 internal cases are already spent
what_the_repair_does_not_do: it does not re-classify a paid start as unspent
it does not re-run any case that already produced paid output
it does not spend a solver start
it does not widen any optimizer cap

attempts_that_spent_nothing.what_happened: after the ledger repair and a fresh A5 PASS, the repaired run died on its first planned case with 'TypeError: object of type int has no len()' inside attempt_refine, before the charge and before the solver was spawned
attempts_that_spent_nothing.root_cause: o0_eval.make_case() returns alpha_points as the count of alpha points, and the new pre-charge code read it as the list; the charge therefore threw while computing its own amount, which is the one way a pre-charge can still lose a start
attempts_that_spent_nothing.what_it_cost: nothing: the failure happened before the charge was written and before any VSPAERO process was spawned. The ledger still reads 3 starts / 39 internal cases and every new case directory holds preparation files only, with no polar and no case_result.json
attempts_that_spent_nothing.how_it_is_closed: the planned cost is now computed by planned_internal_for(), which accepts either the count or the list and is tested without a solver; two further tests pin the wiring: the kind comes from the plan and never from a wake count, and repeat cases are planned at the reference wake mesh of 8
attempts_that_spent_nothing.how_it_is_prevented_from_recurring: o0_final_selftest.py covers the cost helper, the explicit kind wiring and the non-admissibility of wake rows; it runs 12 checks with zero solver starts

o0_final.extra_budget: no extra optimizer starts are spent beyond the O0 search cap; the 8 verification starts above are a separate itemized ledger that cannot propose or admit a new design, and anything beyond them must be requested as another limited batch

not_authorized: any VSPAERO start before the A5 verdict and the Lead GO record
any change to the lift tolerance, target lift or reference quantities
re-use of an old GO or an old authorization id

carried_forward.counting_rule: the latest AUTHORIZATION_CUMULATIVE record is the floor because its counters already include what it carried forward; only batch-local records it did not absorb are added, so nothing is counted twice

batch_budget_statement: the caps below bind the authorization id, not one process. What the authorization can actually spend is min(stored cap, design cap x per-design cost) = 24 starts and 240 internal cases, because the design cap binds first. 23 solver start(s) and 227 internal alpha case(s) are already spent under this authorization, so a GO can authorize at most 1 further starts, 13 further internal cases and 0 further design attempts. No further optimizer design may be proposed: the design cap is spent, so the residue of 1 start(s) and 13 internal case(s) is stranded rather than available. The only physics this pre-registration leaves for authorisation is the separate O0-FINAL verification budget recorded under o0_final.
